MUSIC ACTIVITIES
 Week: Lesson:
 SCHOOL GRADE DATE TIME ROLL
 TWO
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: CREATING/COMPOSING MUSIC
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Rhythm awareness
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:-
 a) Identify animals and objects that make rhythmic patterns for rhythm awareness.
 b) Mimic animals and objects that make rhythmic patterns for rhythm awareness.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 1. Which items make the same beat many times?

LEARNING RESOURCES:
  Items that produce constant beat like a clock.
  Simple recording equipment such as smart phones.
  Relevant songs.
  Relevant recorded rhythms.
  Flash cards.
  KLB Visionary Music Activities Grade 2 Teachers guide pg. 64-67.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Group/individual work.
INTRODUCTION
Learners to identify animals that make rhythmic patterns.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Guide the learners on safety precautions of the instruments to be used.
 Step 2: Guide learners on key words and expressions the learner will interact with in the lesson.
 Step 3: Learners to undergo activities of identifying animals that make rhythmic patterns.
 Step 4: Display pictures of an elephant and clock and show sounds they make.
 SUMMARY:
 Make summary by asking learners to name animals and objects that make rhythms naturally.
 CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
 Learners to practice making rhythmic patterns naturally either by clapping or as directed by the teacher.
 EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
 Learners to practice making rhythmic patterns both at home and at school.
REFLECTION ON THE LESSON/SELF-REMARKS

 TWO
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: CREATING/COMPOSING MUSIC
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Rhythm patterns
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to create simple rhythmic patterns with short and ling
sounds and silences (rests) using body percussion for enjoyment.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 1. Which animals in the environment make repeated rhythmic sounds?
 2. Which machines/objects make repetitive rhythmic patterns?

ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Group/individual work.
INTRODUCTION
Learners to clap/vocalize rhythms of syllables in names.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Guide the learners through activities of clapping syllables in names.e.g tea, mango.
 Step 2: Guide the learners through activities of clapping and vocalizing syllables in names.
 Step 3: Learners to create simple rhythmic patterns that contain sounds of the same value.
 Step 4: Learners to create simple rhythmic patterns that contain sounds of different value.
 SUMMARY:
 Learners to identify the lengths of sounds in words.
 CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to practice by clapping
 EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
 Learners to the activities of creating and imitating rhythms both at school and at home.

SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Rhythmic accompaniment to songs
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:-
 a) create rhythmic accompaniment to familiar songs as a basis for composition.
 b) Record own created rhythms on digital devises to make improvements after listening and for digital
 literacy.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 1. Which animals in the environment make repeated rhythmic sounds?

 Step 1: Guide the learners through activities of creating own rhythms by tapping/clapping to accompany

 TWO
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: CREATING/COMPOSING MUSIC
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Melody (identifying melodic variation)
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to identify melodic variations in familiar tunes in
preparation for creating own songs and for enjoyments.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 a) Which variations can be introduced in a song to make it more interesting?
 b) Which songs are performed loudly or softly?
 c) Why are songs performed slowly?
 CORE COMPETENCIES VALUES PERTINENT CONTEMPORARY ISSUES
 (PCIs)
  Communication and  life skills
 collaboration  decision making skills
  love
  Creativity and imagination  financial literacy
  Responsibility
  Digital literacy  citizenship
  unity
  Self-efficacy
LEARNING RESOURCES:
  A repertoire of simple tunes.
  ICT devices and equipment.
  KLB Visionary Music Activities Grade 2 Teachers guide pg. 77-78.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Group/individual work.
INTRODUCTION
Guide the learners to sing familiar songs for warm up.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Guide the learners to sing familiar tunes to set the right mood for the lesson.
 Step 2: Learners to sing and hum the tune with some variations and let them repeat or imitate the new
 tunes with the variations.e.g. The song “twende sokoni”
 Step 3: Learners to identify sections of melodic variations through singing them out.
 SUMMARY:
 Ask learners questions on the identification of melodic variations.
 CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
 Learners to sing tunes with tempo and dynamic variations
 EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to record their own performances that have sections of melodic repetitions at home.

 MUSIC ACTIVITIES
 Week: Lesson:
 SCHOOL GRADE DATE TIME ROLL
 TWO
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: CREATING/COMPOSING MUSIC
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Improvising simple melodic variations
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:-
 a) Improvise simple melodic variations to familiar tunes as foundation for composition and for
 enjoyment.
 b) Appreciate own and others composition.
 c) Record and play back own variations to familiar songs for preservation, enjoyment and for digital
 literacy.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 a) How can familiar tune be made more interesting?
 b) Why do we make variations to tunes?
 c) How can we make variations to known tunes?
 CORE COMPETENCIES VALUES PERTINENT CONTEMPORARY ISSUES
 (PCIs)
  Communication and  life skills
 collaboration  decision making skills
  love
  Creativity and imagination  financial literacy
  Responsibility
  Digital literacy  citizenship
  unity
  Self-efficacy
LEARNING RESOURCES:
  A repertoire of simple tunes.
  ICT devices such as mobile phones, laptops, tablets.
  KLB Visionary Music Activities Grade 2 Teachers guide pg. 78-79
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Group/individual work.
INTRODUCTION
Learners to sing a familiar song.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Choose TWO or two of the learners to sing a familiar song and guide them to make variations as
 others sing back.
 Step 2: Learners to work in groups by choosing a group leader to lead by singing with some variations as
 the rest in the group imitates.
 Step 3: Give directions on recording of the melodies created for each group using ICT devices.
 Step 4: learners to play back the melodies for appreciation and preservation.
SUMMARY
Summarize the lesson by posing questions on what the learners have learnt.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Observe and listen to learners as they create melodic variations in well-known tunes.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to practice recording of tunes before their parents at home.

 TWO
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: CREATING/COMPOSING MUSIC
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Improvising lyrics/texts to tunes
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:-
 a) Improvise new words to known tunes for creativity and enjoyment.
 b) Appreciate own and others’ composition.
 c) Record and play back their recordings for enjoyment and digital literacy.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 1. How can familiar tune be made more interesting?
 2. Why do we make variations to tunes?
 3. How can we make variations to known tunes?

ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Group/individual work.
INTRODUCTION
Learners to sing a familiar song for introduction.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Learners to sing familiar song then set other words to the same song.
 Step 2: Learners to prepare to repeat or imitate the changes. E.g. “Are you sleeping Brother John”
 Step 3: Learners to record new creations with the new words using ICT devices.
 Step 4: Learners to play back own recordings and others’ for appreciation.
 SUMMARY:
 Listen to learners creations of new words to familiar tunes.
 CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to continue creating new lyrics to tunes and record them.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to carry out an out of class activity as directed by the teacher.

 MUSIC ACTIVITIES
 Week: Lesson:
 SCHOOL GRADE DATE TIME ROLL
 TWO
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: CREATING/COMPOSING MUSIC
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Making presentations of own compositions
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:-
 a) Appreciate own and others’ compositions.
 b) Use digital devices to play own variations to familiar songs for enjoyment and digital literacy.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 1. How did you make changes to the tunes?
 2. How did you make the new words to put into the known tunes?

INTRODUCTION
Guide learners to sing a familiar song for warm up.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Organize learners in preparation for presentation.

 Step 3: After learners presentation, discuss with the learners and the rest of the class give feedback.

 Summarize the lesson by learners asking questions.

 Learners to sing familiar song of own choice for perfection.

Learners to practice adjudication both at school and at home.
